status: registered before any run (a smoke follows)
question: Gemini 4's suggestion and the program's open tangent: apply the subspace floor of e645b to multi-dimensional features. Are the blocks one builds from a public sparse autoencoder, in the manner of Engels et al. 2024, anchored in the native write rows beyond a spectrum-matched null, and are the anchored ones the ones whose activity on text clears its own rotation floor?
design: GPT-2 small (Bloom's residual autoencoder, input of block 7) and Pythia-160m (EleutherAI TopK, after layer 6); 240 wikitext-2 passages of 64 tokens split into a half for the state covariance and a held-out half; live features clustered by spherical k-means (400 clusters), the 150 largest with 9 or more members; each cluster's top-d span for d 2, 4, 8 is a block. Anchoring: largest squared projection of the unit write rows of blocks 0 (or 1) to 6 against 40 rotations of the block inside bands of 16 principal components; anchored at a percentile of 0.95 or more. State side: on held-out states, the share whose projection beats the 95th percentile of the block's rotations at that state, when a member feature fires and when none does. Control: the weekday class-mean subspace and ring at the same depth.

A1.text: the weekday class-mean subspace at the autoencoder's depth is anchored without block 0 in both models

A2.text: at most half of the autoencoder blocks are anchored without block 0, at every d, in both models

A3.text: the anchored fraction is larger at d = 8 than at d = 2 in both models

A4.text: when their features fire, anchored blocks clear their rotation floor more often than unanchored blocks (median), at every d, in both models

A5.text: the blocks' activity is mostly real: the median block clears its rotation floor in half or more of the states where its features fire, at d = 2, in both models

honest_guess: Autoencoder features sit near the rows that write them (e495), so most cluster blocks contain a row deep inside them and are anchored at every d; the weekday subspace is anchored at this depth; when active, anchored blocks clear their rotation floor more often than unanchored ones, and inactive states rarely do.
where_it_ought_to_break: k-means on unit decoder directions is a cruder grouping than Engels' spectral clustering, so the blocks are approximations of theirs
a block built from features that sit on rows is anchored almost by construction; the interesting cases are the blocks that are not
the state side depends on the corpus; wikitext is one register
